name: French Defense
description: Solid defence: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5, then hit the centre with …c5.

lines.name: Advance Variation

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.11: …c4 clamps the queenside, taking b3 and d3 away from White.

lines.summary: Attack the base of the chain: …c5, …Nc6 and …Qb6 all hit d4.

lines.name: 6.a3 c4 7.Be2

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.11: …c4 clamps the queenside, taking b3 and d3 away from White.
notes.13: …Na5 heads for b3, a strong square White can no longer guard with a pawn.

lines.summary: After …c4, the queenside is Black's: aim the knight at b3 and keep White's b4 in check.

lines.name: 6.a3 c4 7.Nbd2

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.11: …c4 clamps the queenside, taking b3 and d3 away from White.
notes.15: …Bd7: the same position as the 7.Be2 order.

lines.summary: 7.Nbd2 and 7.Be2 lead to the same position: …Na5 and …Bd7 either way.

lines.name: Milner-Barry (6.Bd3)

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.10: Bd3 develops and offers the d4 pawn: the Milner-Barry Gambit.
notes.13: …Bd7 first: taking on d4 now loses the queen to Bb5+.

lines.summary: Against 6.Bd3, trade on d4 and play …Bd7 before taking anything: Bb5+ is the trap.

lines.name: Milner-Barry Gambit

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.10: Bd3 develops and offers the d4 pawn: the Milner-Barry Gambit.
notes.13: …Bd7 first: taking on d4 now loses the queen to Bb5+.
notes.15: …Nxd4 takes the offered pawn, now that Bb5+ is covered.
notes.19: …a6 stops Nb5, which would hit the queen and c7.

lines.summary: With …Bd7 in, the d4 pawn is safe to take; then …a6 stops Nb5.

lines.name: Milner-Barry: 8.Bc2

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.10: Bd3 develops and offers the d4 pawn: the Milner-Barry Gambit.
notes.13: …Bd7 first: taking on d4 now loses the queen to Bb5+.
notes.15: …Nb4 hits the c2 bishop and eyes d3.

lines.summary: If White keeps the bishop with Bc2, jump into b4 with the knight.

lines.name: 6.Be2

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 strikes at d4, the base of White's pawn chain.
notes.9: …Qb6 piles up on d4 and eyes the b2 pawn.
notes.11: …cxd4 opens the c-file and leaves d4 without its c3 support.
notes.13: …Nh6 heads for f5, where the knight attacks d4.
notes.15: …Nf5 adds a third attacker on d4, next to the c6 knight and the b6 queen.

lines.summary: Trade on d4, then bring the g8 knight via h6 to f5 to pile up on the d4 pawn.

lines.name: Exchange Variation

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …exd5 gives a symmetrical structure, and Black's light-squared bishop is free.
notes.9: …Bd6 mirrors White's development; the position is level.

lines.summary: Symmetrical and calm: develop naturally and castle.

lines.name: Winawer Variation

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, adding pressure on e4.
notes.7: …c5 hits the d4 pawn, the classic French counter.
notes.9: …Bxc3+ gives up the bishop to double White's c-pawns.
notes.11: …Ne7 develops and keeps the f-pawn free; the knight can go to f5 or c6.

lines.summary: Pin with …Bb4, hit d4 with …c5, then trade on c3 to damage White's pawns.

lines.name: 7.Qg4 (Poisoned Pawn)

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, adding pressure on e4.
notes.7: …c5 hits the d4 pawn, the classic French counter.
notes.9: …Bxc3+ gives up the bishop to double White's c-pawns.
notes.11: …Ne7 develops and keeps the f-pawn free; the knight can go to f5 or c6.
notes.12: Qg4 attacks g7, which the dark-squared bishop no longer defends.
notes.13: …Qc7 counterattacks e5 and c3 instead of defending g7.
notes.17: …cxd4 opens the c-file; Black gives kingside pawns for a strong centre attack.
notes.21: …Bd7 prepares …O-O-O, so the black king hides on the queenside.

lines.summary: Let White take g7 and h7: hit c3 and the centre, then castle long.

lines.name: 7.Nf3

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, adding pressure on e4.
notes.7: …c5 hits the d4 pawn, the classic French counter.
notes.9: …Bxc3+ gives up the bishop to double White's c-pawns.
notes.11: …Ne7 develops and keeps the f-pawn free; the knight can go to f5 or c6.
notes.13: …Nbc6 adds pressure on d4 against White's quiet set-up.

lines.summary: Against the quiet 7.Nf3, keep hitting d4 with …Nbc6; …b6 and …Ba6 to trade bishops is also good.

lines.name: Open (3…c5)

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.5: …c5 hits the centre at once; Black accepts an isolated d-pawn for active pieces.
notes.9: …Nc6 develops and adds pressure on d4.

lines.summary: Meet 3.Nd2 with …c5: active pieces in return for an isolated d-pawn.

lines.name: 2.Nf3

notes.1: …e6 prepares …d5, with a pawn ready to recapture on d5.
notes.3: …d5 claims the centre, just as against 2.d4.
notes.5: …exd5: when White plays d4, this is the Exchange Variation.

lines.summary: Against 2.Nf3, still play …d5; after exd5 exd5 it's an Exchange French.
